doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Hating TV work and the rock acts on the show
summary: Better money but poor music; Quincy Jones with Springsteen and Dylan; Peter and Gordon and other pop acts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Well how did you like working a steady thing, a T.V. show every day?

Oh, I hated it. Just hated it. And then I went out to the coast and he tripled the money. The money was lousy in New York believe it or not. And we went out to the coast, and he more than tripled it. So we made good money out there. But it was even worse. It was awful. It’s a Sonny & Cher world out there, that television. It was people with no ability at all and no talent at all. Did you happen to watch the thing the other day, Quincy Jones trying to teach Bruce Springsteen and the poet/singer, what the hell’s his name, Dylan.

Trying to show them a song. These guys, well you might as well try to talk to that wall to get these guys to hear, they’re totally deaf. It was the most embarrassing thing I’ve ever seen. “Honey come in here. Watch this.” And my wife started laughing, I started laughing, we called up people, “Watch these two idiots.” Millionaires, billionaires these guys. They can’t do anything. God they were awful. Then poor Quincy, he just said okay, fine you know. We’ll just do it your way. Showing them the melody, they just couldn’t get the melody. And so he goes, “Sing what you’re singing. know. Poor Quincy. He’s dealt with these fools for years. And Phil Ramone is in with them too. You know he’s the best sound engineer there is. I don’t know what he’s doing with these guys. Making a lot of money I guess. But he did a lot of great stuff with Woody you know. Great stuff. He’s a hell of a nice guy too. But yeah, it was awful that stuff they were doing. And that’s what used to appear on the show all the time. Monty Rock III. The Lovin’ Spoonful. And what was a couple of others. Peter and something or other, no, when the Beatle thing was going on.
Peter and — Chad and Jeremy, Peter and Gordon.
Peter and Gordon. Oh, man, I mean they were awful.
And you had to play behind them.

Oh yeah, and, “No that’s too—” and, “well don’t try to fix it up fellas” the trumpet player says “just play it as bad as they want it. I told you it wasn’t going to be fun.” And this is awful. Then Benny Goodman would come on and it would be fine. Count Basie’d come on, it was a great show. Bill Watrous got him to come on, the trombone player.
